clue.text: Spare money to get drugs

parts.note: bucks are dollars, slang for money
H is heroin and E is ecstasy, here E twice for two doses: drugs in the plural

explanation.surface: Someone diverts their spare cash to buy narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spare money' reads as one phrase, but 'Spare' alone is the definition. H (heroin) and E (ecstasy) are standard crossword drug abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckshee is British slang for free or surplus, something going spare at no cost.

clue.text: Writer leaving diamonds as down payment

indicators.note: leaving says the diamonds letter goes out of the writer's name

parts.note: Dante, the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: An author abandons their jewels to put down a deposit.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is the stake put up in advance in poker, a payment made before play begins.

clue.text: See 24
Sow eating cow's food on the beach?

indicators.note: eating says the first word swallows the second, holding it inside

parts.note: to sow is to seed a field
to cow is to intimidate, to fill with awe

explanation.surface: A female pig munching what a cow might eat by the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sow' and 'cow' look like farm animals, but sow is the verb (plant) and cow the verb (overawe); the 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Kelp and wrack wash up on the shore, a cryptic picture of shoreline fodder; the question mark flags the playful sense.

clue.text: Furniture maker adapted thrones to accommodate Camilla's bottom

indicators.note: to accommodate means the rearranged letters take another inside them
adapted says the letters of thrones are altered into a new order
bottom is the last letter of the name, as this is a down clue's base

explanation.surface: A cabinetmaker reshapes royal seats to fit the Queen's posterior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' rearranges THRONES into SHERTON, which takes in the A at the end of Camilla.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Sheraton was an eighteenth-century English cabinetmaker whose name became a furniture style.

clue.text: English verse found in account book

indicators.note: found in says the pair of letters sits inside the account word

parts.note: a relation is a narrative or account of events

explanation.surface: A line of English poetry turns up in a ledger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'account book' looks like a ledger, but 'account' is wordplay and 'book' alone the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The final book of the New Testament carries this name, the Apocalypse of John.

clue.text: Germ found by American carer in barge

indicators.note: in places the carer inside the barge

parts.note: a keel is a flat-bottomed coal barge, especially on the Tyne
RN is a registered nurse, the usual US term

explanation.surface: A microbe discovered by a US nurse on a canal boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Germ' suggests infection but means the seed or core.
explanation.definitionFit: Germ in the sense of seed or core, as in the germ of an idea.

clue.text: Go to staff barrier

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in 'your go'
a pike is a long-shafted weapon, a staff

explanation.surface: An instruction to head for the staff barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a turnpike was the toll gate across a road, a barrier lifted on payment.

clue.text: See 24
Tree put back in Greek arboretum

indicators.note: put back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tree is replanted in a Greek tree garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The hiding is unsignalled beyond 'in': EEKA sits across 'Greek arboretum' and 'put back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The akee is a West African tree whose fruit is eaten in Jamaica with saltfish.

clue.text: Relatives welcoming role we developed for US city

indicators.note: welcoming says the relatives take the other letters in

parts.note: nans are grandmothers

indicators.note: developed says the letters of role we are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Family members welcome a part we've built up, for an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relatives' are grandmothers here, not any kin; 'developed' is the signal to rearrange 'role we'.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisiana's largest city, the birthplace of jazz, on the Mississippi.

clue.text: Question about stray in boat

indicators.note: about says the question goes around the straying word

parts.note: why is a question word
to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: A query about a wandering animal found in a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A wherry is a light rowing boat or a broad Norfolk sailing barge.

clue.text: Utter cad is furious to be sent down from university

indicators.note: furious suggests wild, violent motion, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A scoundrel is enraged at being expelled from college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like an adjective, but it is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: At Oxford and Cambridge, to rusticate a student is to suspend them, sending them away to the country.

clue.text: Old nurses keeping track of body parts

indicators.note: keeping says the nurses hold the track inside

parts.note: ENs were enrolled nurses, a grade of British nursing now phased out
a trail is a track

explanation.surface: Elderly nurses keeping a record of anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrails are the intestines and inner organs, body parts within the abdomen.

clue.text: Saviour of old Thailand briefly trapped in net

indicators.note: trapped in says the shortened name is caught inside the net

parts.note: mesh is netting

indicators.note: briefly says the name is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: Siam was the former name of Thailand

explanation.surface: A rescuer from old Thailand, quickly caught in a net.
explanation.definitionFit: The Messiah is the promised deliverer, Christ in Christian belief, a saviour.

clue.text: Colour of tip of asparagus and thyme sprinkled on pastry filling

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter
sprinkled says the herb's letters are scattered into a new order
the filling of pastry is its centre, the two middle letters

explanation.surface: A recipe: asparagus tips and thyme scattered over a pastry filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sprinkled' rearranges THYME into METHY; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Amethyst is a purple-violet shade named after the quartz gemstone.

clue.text: Auctioneer's first new customer ignoring large antique

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the auctioneer
ignoring says the large letter is left out of the customer word

parts.note: a client is a customer
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: At a sale, an auctioneer overlooks a big new buyer for an old piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient and antique are both adjectives meaning very old, from a long-past age.

clue.text: Transport turned up with something used to carry baby

indicators.note: turned up, in a down clue, says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to run someone somewhere is to transport them
a sling is a strap for carrying a baby or an arm

explanation.surface: A vehicle arrives with a baby carrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reads like 'arrived', but in a down clue it reverses the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursling is an infant still being nursed, a baby at the breast.

clue.text: Do away with edges of elegant heraldic device

parts.note: to annul is to cancel or abolish

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Getting rid of the frills on an elegant coat of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry an annulet is a small ring used as a charge on a shield.

clue.text: Middle-Easterner is related to Italian mathematician

definitions.meaning: a native of Galilee, the region in northern Israel
an adjective for Galileo Galilei's work

explanation.surface: A person from the Levant turns out to be kin to an Italian scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names someone from Galilee and describes things connected with Galileo.

clue.text: Republican leaving mass meetings to supporters

indicators.note: leaving says the Republican letter goes out of the gatherings

parts.note: rallies are large public gatherings

explanation.surface: A Republican abandons big political gatherings for their backers.
explanation.definitionFit: Allies are those who back and stand with you, supporters in a cause.

clue.text: Watch posted on risky boundaries

parts.note: sent means posted, as a letter

indicators.note: the boundaries of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A wristwatch sent off on dangerous borders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' suggests a timepiece but means a guard; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch can be a person on guard duty, just as a sentry keeps watch.

clue.text: Goad batsman with beginnings of slight advantage

indicators.note: beginnings of picks the opening letters of slight

parts.note: an edge is an advantage over a rival

explanation.surface: Taunting a batsman for a small lead.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, sledging is taunting the batsman to break their concentration.
explanation.definitionFit: To sledge is cricket slang for needling the opposing batsman with insults.

clue.text: Classic work: book associated with escape close to Scottish river

parts.note: a leak is an escape of gas or water

indicators.note: close to a word means its final letter

parts.note: the Ouse is an English river, a standard crossword river

explanation.surface: A classic book connected with a getaway near a Scottish river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to Scottish river' suggests a Scottish river, but 'close to' takes only Scottish's last letter, and the Ouse is in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleak House is a Dickens novel, a classic of English literature.

clue.text: Method defining new director and silent film maker

indicators.note: defining is read as setting bounds round, so the method encloses the rest

parts.note: a way is a method

indicators.note: new says the letters are made over into a fresh order

explanation.surface: An approach defines a new director and a silent-movie maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defining' is used in its sense of marking the limits, so the method word goes round; 'new' signals rearranging the director letter with 'silent'.
explanation.definitionFit: Walt Disney founded the animation studio behind Mickey Mouse, a film maker who began in the silent era.

clue.text: Spring cured so-called rich

parts.note: a well is a spring of water

indicators.note: so-called signals that the word is as spoken, a sound-alike

parts.note: healed means cured

explanation.surface: A spa treatment supposedly cured the wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-heeled is an idiom for prosperous, wealthy enough for good shoes.

clue.text: Australian leaving several dodgy bars

indicators.note: leaving says the Australian letter is taken away from the pool
dodgy suggests something unreliable, so the remaining letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An Australian walks out of several shady pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: SEVERAL less A, rearranged ('dodgy'), gives the answer; 'bars' looks like pubs but means rods.
explanation.definitionFit: Levers are rigid bars used to pivot and prise, crowbars and the like.

clue.text: Grand scheme essential to get exotic fruit

indicators.note: essential to means the pieces sit at the heart of the other word
exotic suggests something strange, so the letters of get are rearranged

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
a plan is a scheme

explanation.surface: A big plan vital to obtaining unusual fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' looks like it describes the fruit but is the signal to rearrange 'get' into EGT; 'essential to' puts the grand scheme at its heart.
explanation.definitionFit: The aubergine is botanically a berry, so the fruit of the plant; Americans call it eggplant.
